macro.headline: Bull regime intact, but breadth narrowing and momentum diverging from price.
macro.story:
The tape is up — SPY, QQQ, Nasdaq, Dow, and Russell 2000 all sit above their 50- and 200-day moving averages, with the small-caps leading on a 21-day basis (+8.5%). That's classic late-cycle bull behavior: risk-on rotating into the riskier corners. But underneath the price strength, the momentum indicators are telling a more cautious story. MACD is below signal on SPY, QQQ, and Nasdaq even as price makes new highs — a classic momentum divergence that says the rally is decelerating, not accelerating.

The dominant cross-asset catalyst, grounded in the active themes, is the AI Infrastructure capex cycle (CHASING stage, conviction 8). Capital is concentrating into mega-cap compute and the platform layer, funded — as the theme adjacency notes — by an unwind of defensive hedges: gold is down ~7% over 21 days, silver -12%, and the dollar (DXY) is overbought-extended at RSI 71 with a validated inverse pull on metals. That's the dollar-strength → commodity-headwind edge playing out in real time. Layer on the Geopolitical Risk Unwind theme (Iran/Hormuz) and you get WTI crude down ~24% over 21 days into RSI 30 — a disinflationary tailwind that supports growth multiples but crushes the Energy sector.

Rates are the wildcard. The 10Y-2Y spread has collapsed -53% over 21 days as the 2Y yield pushes overbought (RSI 63) — a flattening that historically pressures Financials' net interest margins, even as the sector trades HOT here. VIX at 17.2 is benign, term structure in contango (VIX3M/VIX = 1.19), and the Engine C washout state is CALM — no timing edge active. So the regime is bullish, but the confidence is capped at MEDIUM because of the MACD divergence on the major indices, narrow S&P breadth (only 29% bullish vs 43% bearish), and only 5 of 11 sectors above their 50-day. This is a market where you hunt longs in the hot rotation pockets — not a blanket risk-on.

active.name: AI Infrastructure Build-Out — Mega-Cap Compute & Software
active.thesis: Institutional capital is concentrating into the AI compute stack — silicon (NVDA, INTC), infrastructure software (MSFT, PLTR), and the platform/ad layer monetizing inference (META, AAPL). With VIX at 15.88, bullish put/call, and SPY above 50SMA, the TRANSITIONAL regime is being expressed through quality mega-cap tech rather than broad risk-on, suggesting capital is rotating UP the quality curve rather than out.
active.evidence: XLK accel_ratio 1.715 and QQQ accel_ratio 3.323 (14d bull rate 3.3x the 60d baseline) show genuine fresh acceleration, not just persistence. Software-Infrastructure (1.992) and Consumer Electronics (2.246) are leading the doubling-up.

invalidators.condition: XLK sector trajectory shifts to FADING_BULLISH or bearish
Software-Infrastructure or Semis industry trajectory degrades to HOLDING_BULLISH or below
FOMC (6/10) or CPI (6/11) prints hawkish surprise, DXY accelerates higher and breaks rate-sensitive growth multiples
14d/60d accel ratio falls below 1.0 across XLK industries
Lottery strike flow % crosses above 18% (retail blow-off signal)

active.name: Natural Gas Reversal — Early Commodity Flip
active.thesis: Natural gas has flipped from ACCELERATING_BEARISH to bullish (+0.37%/day 14d) while crude oil and broader energy commodities (USO, BNO, DBC) are flipping the other way — a divergence that historically signals supply-side gas tightening (storage draw, weather, or LNG export demand) independent of macro oil weakness. Early-stage and contrarian to the broader commodity tape.
active.evidence: UNG is the ONLY commodity in the universe with a bearish-to-bullish flip; every other energy and ag commodity is rolling over. The asymmetry is the signal — but 60d base is still -9.96%, so this is an inflection trade, not a confirmed trend.

invalidators.condition: UNG trajectory returns to DIRECTION_FLIP_bullish_to_bearish or ACCELERATING_BEARISH
EIA weekly storage report prints materially above estimates (bearish surprise)
14d rate decelerates below +0.15%/day for 5 consecutive sessions

active.name: Geopolitical Risk Unwind — Iran Deal / Hormuz Reopening
active.thesis: The Iran nuclear deal and the Strait of Hormuz reopening have resolved near-term crude supply-disruption risk. WTI crude has fallen approximately 5% to near $80/barrel as the geopolitical risk premium unwinds. This is unambiguously RISK-ON for equities: lower crude reduces input-cost and inflation-expectation pressure, eases the case for further Fed tightening, and removes the dominant macro tail-risk from the narrative. The correct read on oil weakness here is NOT 'Iran re-escalation risk' — it is the OPPOSITE: the Hormuz corridor is reopening and supply constraints are lifting. Energy equities (XLE, E&P names) face near-term margin compression from lower realized prices, but the broader equity market benefits. Transports and consumer discretionary are direct fuel-cost beneficiaries.
active.evidence: WTI crude ~$80 (-~5% from recent highs); crude trajectory shifting from HOLDING_BULLISH toward FADING_BULLISH/bearish. Natural gas divergence intact (independent supply story — not demand-driven). Broad commodity complex already fading (DBC, USO, BNO).

invalidators.condition: Iran deal collapses or Hormuz incidents resume — crude reverses sharply higher
OPEC+ emergency production cut to defend $80 floor offsets supply increase

newsletter:
**[THE SPINE]** Dollar strength is the dominant force this week, and it is doing real work across the tape. DXY at 100.85 sits above its upper Bollinger band with RSI 71.6, +1.8% on the month, +2.0% over its 50SMA — and the backtested DXY_METALS_TAG signal is ACTIVE. That single force is simultaneously crushing the metals complex, capping commodity reflation themes, and quietly reinforcing the rotation back into US large-cap tech and industrials.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The macro backdrop confirms rather than threatens the spine. Regime is CHOPPY (6/10, transitional), but VIX 17.1 in contango with VIX3M 19.6 says no stress bid. The 2Y at 3.67 (RSI 73) and 10Y at 4.50 are firm — and per the backtest, the 10Y has no ceiling edge to lean on, so treat yields as trending, not capped. Gold -7.1% on 21d, Silver -12.0%, Oil -24.0% with WTI RSI 29.6 — and remember WTI mean-reversion has no edge (T2 oversold kept falling), so oversold is just a trend tag, not a buy signal. The DXY-metals inverse (corr -0.45, sustained in 70% of rolling 24-month windows) is doing exactly what the tape needs it to do.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Money is flowing into dollar-insensitive, domestic-revenue growth and cyclicals. XLK +10.5% on 21d (ACCELERATING_BULLISH), IWM +8.5%, XLI +7.2%, XLB +5.7%, QQQ +5.6%, XLF +4.8% — leaders are tech, small caps, industrials, materials, financials. Out of the picture: defensive utilities (+0.9%) and the entire precious/broad commodity complex, both flagged FADING. Rotation INTO Consumer Electronics, Software - Infrastructure, and unmapped (AI-adjacent) names; nothing notable rotating out, which is itself a tell — this is a one-way flow week.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** Semiconductors are the textbook extended trade: HOT 13 months, +258% — the largest run on record — and explicitly flagged CEILING. That is exit management territory, not entry. The in-range setups are in Software - Infrastructure (HOT 1 mo, only +3%, early innings vs typical 7-month / +18% spell) and Internet Content & Information (HOT 1 mo, still -5%, early vs typical 6-month spell) — both ACCELERATING/HOLDING bullish with runway. Metal Fabrication (HOT 6 mo, +20%, above-typical but not extreme) fits the industrials bid. Avoid chasing Consumer Electronics despite the 2.25 accel — it is -12.4% on 21d, which is a washout bounce profile, and 88% of washout lows get retested within 60 days.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** DXY 98.88 support is the tripwire. A clean break below it cracks the spine — metals catch a bid, the FADING commodity themes get a second look, and the small-cap/industrials leadership likely broadens further. As long as DXY holds above 98.88 with RSI north of 60, lean with the dollar-strength regime: tech and domestic cyclicals over metals, miners, and energy. Breadth at 24% bullish / 50% bearish in the S&P is the soft spot — if leadership narrows further into just semis, the spine is intact but the index gets fragile.
